summary.text: Lisa Borowski is a Democratic state representative who has represented Pennsylvania House of Representatives District 168 since December 1, 2022 and is on the ballot for re-election on November 3, 2026.
A former Radnor school board member and township commissioner, she lists health care access, first responders and public education among her priorities.

paragraphs.text: Lisa Borowski was born in Darby, Pennsylvania, and earned a bachelor's degree from Drexel University in 1989.
Her career experience includes working as a communications director.

In a 2026 Ballotpedia survey, she said she became involved in politics in 2010 during a Radnor school board budget debate, ran for the school board and won, and later served as the board's vice president.
She said she later served as a Radnor Township Commissioner and was elected board president.
Borowski assumed office in the state House in December 2022.

In the 2023-2024 session she was assigned to the Aging and Older Adult Services, Committee on Committees, Consumer Protection and Professional Licensure, Health, and Veterans Affairs and Emergency Preparedness committees.
In the same survey she named health care access and affordability, support for volunteer fire and EMS providers and state police staffing, and climate and renewable energy among her key messages.
